summary.name: On Being On Call
summary.one_liner: A blog post arguing that developers learn valuable lessons from being on call for their own production code, but that on-call duty must be an explicit, up-front job requirement.
use_cases: Deciding whether to add an on-call rotation to a development team
Evaluating on-call expectations when job hunting
Making the case for developers owning production code
Understanding how on-call shapes software quality
summary.what_it_does: The page is a personal blog essay responding to a Twitter discussion about putting developers on call. The author says being on call teaches developers how their code behaves in production and when it breaks, giving feedback on simplicity, comments, commit messages and failure cases. He argues it fosters DevOps culture and avoids us-vs-them tension with operations teams. He notes Heroku reduces the scope of on-call responsibility for developers. He concludes that on-call should be an explicit requirement stated when hiring, and that adding it later should be handled carefully because some people cannot or will not take it on.
notable: Argues on-call duty should be an explicit, up-front job requirement
Frames on-call as a way to learn how code really behaves in production
Mentions Heroku as a low-scope way for developers to experience on-call
caveats: Opinion essay, not a tool or product; pricing does not apply
Written in 2016 and reflects one author's views
